title: Semidefinite extension complexity of the separable set, with applications to approximate disentanglers
authors: Sevag Gharibian, Carsten Hecht, Dorian Rudolph
abstract: We prove quantitative lower bounds on the semidefinite extension complexity of the set of separable quantum states on $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$. We consider semidefinite programs (SDPs) that approximate the maximum acceptance probability of a measurement over separable states, the optimization problem underlying QMA(2). In the extended-formulation model of Harrow, Natarajan, and Wu (HNW), all measurements share a common feasible region and an objective-independent embedding of product states that exactly reproduces their acceptance probabilities. For every $0<θ<2/7$, there are constants $c_θ,a_θ>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $d$, any such SDP with uniform additive error $0<a\le a_θ$ has size at least $d^{c_θ\min\{a^{-1/3},d^θ\}}$. The bound applies at sufficiently small constant error, is superpolynomial in $d$ whenever $a=o(1)$, and becomes $d^{Ω(d^θ)}$ when $a\le d^{-3θ}$, improving HNW's quasipolynomial bound at inverse- square error. The same bound holds for any SDP-representable convex set of states that contains all separable states and lies within trace distance $a$ of them, giving a quantitative counterpart to Fawzi's theorem that the separable set has no exact semidefinite representation. Our proof combines the quantitative pseudo-density theorem of Lee, Raghavendra, and Steurer with explicit block-positive operators and Chebyshev amplification. Our main results are supported by Lean proofs.
summary: This paper derives strong, quantitative lower bounds on the size of semidefinite programs needed to approximate the set of separable quantum states. By connecting these bounds to the concept of approximate disentanglers, the authors provide a powerful tool to study the computational complexity of quantum information tasks, improving upon previous results in the field.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish quantitative lower bounds on the size of Semidefinite Programs (SDPs) used to approximate the maximum acceptance probability over separable quantum states, which is central to understanding the complexity class QMA(2).
main_result: They prove that the required SDP size grows superpolynomially with the dimension $d$ for constant approximation errors, improving previous bounds significantly.
method: The proof combines the quantitative pseudo-density theorem of Lee, Raghavendra, and Steurer with the extended-formulation model of SDPs, relating the required size to the approximation error.
model_or_system: The focus is on bipartite quantum systems ($\mathbb{C}^d \otimes \mathbb{C}^d$) and the set of separable quantum states, $	ext{Sep}(d:d)$. The context is quantum complexity theory, specifically QMA(2).
key_observables: The maximum acceptance probability $h_{Sep}(Q)$ and the required size ($r$) of the SDP approximation.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$, the additive approximation error $a$, and the entanglement/disentangler errors $\epsilon, \delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the SDP extended-formulation model (HNW) and the existence of an approximate disentangler $\Lambda$ whose failure to perfectly represent the separable set is quantified by the error $a$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives lower bounds on the SDP size required to approximate the separable set, first for the general SDP formulation and then specifically by relating it to the structure imposed by approximate disentanglers.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical tools (SDP complexity bounds) to quantify the computational separation between quantum complexity classes, which is fundamental to understanding the limits of quantum computation.
